cells.tense: You are at the start of something and your hand is on it now.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Take one thing off someone's plate this week — a call made, a ride, a hand with something heavy — and stay until it's done.
cells.core:
Something is beginning near you and you are not spending it to prove anything. You can hold what comes to hand without putting it to work before it has a shape; you let a thing be early without announcing anything about it. That is directed form starting well, and it needs none of your commentary.

Let some of the strength you are sitting on go out to one person this week. Point one real piece of help at a hand that needs it and stay until it is finished. Keep what holds you in reserve; there will still be plenty, and some of that reserve will now belong to whoever received it. This is the direction the start is free to grow in.

cells.tense: You are already braced for a start that has no shape yet.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Before you act on this, put every feeling that comes with it on a page. Nothing ranked, nothing crossed out. Close the page, then move.
cells.core:
Everything here is still open and none of it is committed, and that is not a problem to solve. You want a solid thing now, fully claimed, and you keep arriving at the shape of what is about to begin before the shape exists. The pressure is not coming from the start; it is coming from your rush to finish it.

What is moving toward you comes in every colour at once. Put the whole of what you feel on one page before you do anything: no ranking, no fixing, no sorting into what is allowed. Then close it. Move when the next step is clear, not when the waiting becomes uncomfortable. The feeling gets to be all the way felt first.

cells.tense: A beginning has already gone by and you are not entering it.
cells.ask: Sit with the thing you keep circling. Stay with it until the whole of it is there, including the part you would rather not say. Let it be finished, not fixed.
cells.core:
Where this start is concerned, you stopped showing up and the door closed behind you. The thing is still in your hand but you are not looking at it; you are looking back at somewhere you used to be, and nothing is asking you for anything. Whatever could have begun has already been filed as gone, and that filing is most of what is happening.

You can look at this truly. Sit with whatever you circle and stay until the picture is whole, including the piece you would rather leave out. Not solved, not excused — seen completely. This does not ask you to push effort or warmth into a place that is running low; it asks you to keep going past the point where you usually turn away. Whatever you land on can be the last word on it.

cells.tense: You are making the calls about this start and calling them circumstance.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: Set out what you have already chosen about this start — every piece, on one page — and read it back. Notice your hand in it. Then leave the page alone.
cells.core:
You keep arriving at the edge of something and reading your own hand there as luck. What is already in motion under you stays unnamed, and the part of you that says this is how it happened is the part handing your pen away. You are the one deciding, and nobody has told you so.

Set out what you have already chosen about this start — every piece, on one page. Read it back and see the whole of it, nothing hidden, including the parts you would rather leave to chance. When it is all there in your own hand, leave it alone. Seeing it plainly is the whole of the act today.
